one_line: Recent AI developments include Google's release of Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash with lower pricing and native video creation, a massive funding round and valuation for OpenAI, NVIDIA's new Cosmos 3 open models for interactive world simulation, advancements in agent memory architectures by Anthropic and researchers, and the demonstration of a Firecracker VM escape vulnerability.

stories.title: Google Releases Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash with Lower Pricing and Native Video Creation
stories.summary: Google has made Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash generally available across the Gemini API and Gemini for business with a 30% price drop. The updated model also introduces native video creation for clips up to 15 seconds long.
stories.why_it_matters: You can now generate longer video clips and integrate multimodal capabilities at a lower cost of $0.07 per second for 720p video.
stories.editor_reason: Google introduces Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash, a major new model release for developers.

facts.claim: Google rolled out Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash, making it generally available across the Gemini API and Gemini for business.
facts.quote: Today, we’re rolling out Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash, and making it generally available across the Gemini API and Gemini for business.

facts.claim: The price has been dropped by 30% compared to Gemini Omni 1.1, now priced at $0.07 per second for 720p video.
facts.quote: We have dropped the price 30% from Gemini Omni 1.1 making it available at $0.07 per second for 720p video.

facts.claim: The updated model introduces native video creation for clips up to 15 seconds long, increasing from the previous 10-second limit.
facts.quote: You can now generate and edit videos natively up to 15 seconds long, up from 10 seconds with Omni 1.1.

stories.title: OpenAI Raises $11 Billion at a $1.25 Trillion Valuation
stories.summary: OpenAI has secured $11 billion in a new funding round that values the company at $1.25 trillion. The organization is currently expected to hold an IPO next year following a delay from this year.
stories.why_it_matters: This massive capital injection supports OpenAI's continued scaling as it prepares for a public market debut.
stories.editor_reason: OpenAI reportedly raises $11B in massive funding round at a historic $1.25T valuation.

facts.claim: OpenAI has raised $11 billion in a new funding round.
facts.quote: OpenAI has reportedly raised $11 billion so far in a new funding round

facts.claim: The funding round values OpenAI at $1.25 trillion.
facts.quote: that values the AI lab at $1.25 trillion.

facts.claim: OpenAI is currently expected to hold an IPO next year after delaying plans to go public this year.
facts.quote: There are expectations that the company will IPO next year at some point.

stories.title: NVIDIA Introduces New Cosmos 3 Open Models for Interactive World Simulation
stories.summary: NVIDIA released four new open-weight checkpoints for the Cosmos 3 model family, tailored for interactive world simulation and driving scenes. These post-trained Nano models feature 16 billion trainable parameters and use OpenMDW1.1 for commercial and non-commercial licensing.
stories.why_it_matters: You can utilize these open-weight models under OpenMDW1.1 terms for building simulation and driving applications.
stories.editor_reason: NVIDIA releases Cosmos 3 open models for interactive physical world simulation.

facts.claim: NVIDIA introduced four new open-weight checkpoints to its Cosmos 3 model family for interactive world simulation and driving scenes.
facts.quote: NVIDIA Cosmos world model development platform adds four new open-weight checkpoints to its Cosmos 3 model family

facts.claim: All four new models are post-trained examples of Cosmos 3 Nano and feature 16 billion trainable parameters.
facts.quote: All four models are post-trained examples of Cosmos 3 Nano and have 16B trainable parameters.

facts.claim: The models utilize OpenMDW1.1, which permits both commercial and non-commercial use under its terms.
facts.quote: The models use OpenMDW1.1, permitting commercial and non-commercial use under its terms.

stories.title: New Research Details Agent Memory and Offline Processing Techniques
stories.summary: Researchers proposed sleep-time compute and Anthropic implemented dreaming to help models like Claude reorganize context and maintain effective memory during offline periods. In testing, Claude Opus 5 closed the learning loop on the Continual Learning Bench 1.0, while Claude Sonnet 3.7 successfully managed hundreds of memory files while playing Pokémon Red.
stories.why_it_matters: These memory architectures and offline processing methods enable your AI agents to maintain persistent, long-term state across complex, multi-session tasks.
stories.editor_reason: Anthropic publishes foundational research outlining the architectural components of agent memory.

facts.claim: Researchers at Letta and UC Berkeley proposed sleep-time compute as a way for models to use idle time to reorganize context.
facts.quote: Researchers at Letta and UC Berkeley proposed sleep-time compute as a way for models to use idle time between interactions to reorganize their existing context.

facts.claim: Anthropic uses a process called dreaming to help give Claude effective memory by reflecting on logs during offline periods.
facts.quote: We’ve found that dreaming has been a useful tool for helping us give Claude effective memory.

facts.claim: In tests on the Continual Learning Bench 1.0, Claude Opus 5 was the first model to successfully close the learning loop using memory.
facts.quote: Claude Opus 5 was the first of these models to close the loop.

facts.claim: During a test playing Pokémon Red, Claude Sonnet 3.7 wrote 413 memory files across 225 folders and earned one badge.
facts.quote: Ultimately, Sonnet 3.7 wrote 413 memory files across 225 folders and earned one badge

stories.title: Researchers Demonstrate Firecracker VM Escape via KVM_RUN Vulnerability
stories.summary: Researchers achieved a virtual machine escape from Firecracker, resulting in root code execution on the host system. The exploit, designated as CVE-2026-99999, targets the return from the KVM_RUN system call to hijack saved registers.
stories.why_it_matters: If you rely on Firecracker microVMs for isolation, you must account for this host-level escape vector targeting KVM_RUN.
stories.editor_reason: Critical VM escape vulnerability detailed in Firecracker, widely used for AI sandboxing.

facts.claim: Researchers achieved a VM escape from Firecracker, obtaining root code execution on the host.
facts.quote: We escaped it and achieved code execution as root on the host.

facts.claim: The exploit targets the return from the KVM_RUN system call to hijack the Firecracker thread's saved registers.
facts.quote: That made the return from KVM_RUN an attractive target.

facts.claim: The attack methodology demonstrated a vulnerability identified as CVE-2026-99999.
facts.quote: This is a continuation to show CVE-2026-99999 on a Firecracker setup.
